text:
maria_acharya: Hey all — noticed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate on canary today after the kernel selector change. Overall QPS steady but token latency tail jumps for RAG-style requests. :frowning:

jonathan_b: saw it too during the 11:10 loadtest, 95p latency +120ms on g4dn nodes. Noticed higher eviction counts in kvcache metrics.

ara_patel: any specific workload reproducer? chat vs completion?

maria_acharya: Primarily RAG + structured output (JSON objects appended) and long conversation prefixes (5-12 messages). Chat completions are mostly unaffected. Key observation: prefix key cardinality shot up because we started including dynamic convo metadata ordering in the key after that PR.

jonathan_b: that aligns with my profiler: kernel selection now prefers the new fused-attn kernel for short sequences, but our sequence length distribution shifted (many long prefixes), so we get more kernel switches mid-batch. That increases overhead and causes coalescing to widen batching windows, which in turn increases kvcache churn.

perf-bot: ALERT: prefix_cache_hit_rate dropped from 0.82 -> 0.48 over 10m (service: inference-runtime, hostpool: canary-2) :bangbang:

sam_h: can you paste an example of the actual cache keys we're generating?

maria_acharya: sure — sanitized example: 

```
prefix_key_v3::model=tiny-llama::conv=[u:123|m:345|s:stoned]::metadata_order=[source,session_ts]::shard=0
prefix_key_v2::model=tiny-llama::conv=[u:123|m:345|s:stoned]::shard=0
```

maria_acharya: PR added metadata_order to help determinism for structured outputs, but in practice agents reorder fields when building RAG contexts so almost every request had a different key.

ara_patel: Oof. So key entropy skyrockets. We should normalize metadata by stable-sorting keys and canonicalizing arrays. Also consider dropping ordering from key entirely and instead use a fingerprint of canonicalized metadata.

sam_h: proposed patch (pseudo): 
```
# pseudo
canonical = json.dumps(metadata, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"))
fingerprint = sha1(canonical)[:12]
prefix_key = f"prefix_v4::{model}::{conv_fp}::{fingerprint}"
```

kevin_w: short-term mitigation: can we roll back the kernel-selector change on canary to see if hit-rate recovers? If kernel change is orthogonal, we still need key fix but rollback helps isolate.

maria_acharya: agreed. Plan: 1) rollback kernel-selector to previous commit on canary-2, 2) deploy prefix canonicalization patch behind feature flag, 3) run canary workload generator that simulates RAG with randomized field orders + long contexts, 4) disable aggressive batch coalescing for this pool to avoid warmup churn.

jonathan_b: I can run a quick benchmark: retain exact same batching heuristics but pin kernel. If hit-rate recovers, we know kernel <-> batching interaction is the multiplier. I'll post numbers in ~30m.

ara_patel: also add a regression test to eval harness: create 50k synthetic RAG prefixes with permuted metadata fields and verify kvcache key cardinality stays under threshold. Should be part of CI for prefix-key changes.

maria_acharya: good call. Action items: @jonathan_b run pinned-kernel canary + perf dump; @sam_h open PR for canonical fingerprinting (feature-flagged); @ara_patel add unit/reg test to eval harness; @kevin_w coordinate rollback window & monitor. I'll create the rollout plan doc later. :memo:

perf-bot: NOTE: follow-up alert suppressed for 1h during canary operations.

sam_h: one more thought — for structured outputs we should consider partial-keying: only key by the prefix tokens and the deterministic parts of metadata (like source id), not the entire metadata blob. That reduces sensitivity but keeps correctness for prefix reuse.

maria_acharya: yeah, partial-keying + canonical fingerprint for the rest seems like a good middle ground. We'll measure quality regressions with our eval prompt set (RAG Q/A, slot-filling JSON).

jonathan_b: numbers from the pinned-kernel canary: after rollback, prefix_cache_hit_rate climbed from 0.49 -> 0.79 in 12m, 95p token-latency dropped ~110ms. Eviction_rate dropped 3.4x. Looks like kernel change worsened batching behaviour in presence of high key-cardinality.

kevin_w: ok let's proceed with the flagged prefix canonicalization + partial-key approach, then re-apply the kernel selector change behind a rollout that monitors hit-rate and batching metrics. We should also add a canary test that synthesizes kernel-switching sequences.

ara_patel: I'll add the keys: kvcache_cardinality, eviction_rate, prefix_cache_hit_rate, batching_window_ms to the canary dashboard and set alerts.

maria_acharya: thanks everyone. I'll open the rollout PRs and annotate with repro steps. Will follow up with a short postmortem once we verify fix in prod canary. :+1:

jonathan_b: 👍

ara_patel: :eyes:

sam_h: :hammer_and_wrench:
